marks.gloss_en: (איכא דאמרי) והאנן תנן: בזמן שכנפיה נוגעות בקן -- חייב לשלח!
אמר רב יהודה: כי קתני מתניתין -- בנוגע מן הצד
לאקושי אפרוחים לביצים: the eggs are compared to the fledglings (the mishna, 140b.14: as fledglings are viable, so the eggs must be viable -- addled eggs excluded)
וביצים לאפרוחים: the fledglings are compared to the eggs (the mishna, 140b.14: as eggs need their mother, so the fledglings must need her -- fledglings that fly excluded)
שנאמר קן -- קן מכל מקום: the mishna's own derasha, re-aimed at the fledglings that fly and the addled eggs
אם כן נכתוב קרא והאם רובצת עליהם -- had the verse only meant a plural it would say 'on them'; its naming fledglings and eggs is for the hekesh, so the plural ground of the reversal falls
לאקושי אפרוחים לביצים וביצים לאפרוחים -- the phrase is for the comparison, which is what excludes fledglings that fly and addled eggs; the reversal's second half falls
[and] fledglings that fly or addled eggs -- one is obligated to send, as it is said 'nest' -- a nest in any case
דבעינן אפרוחים או ביצים וליכא -- the verse's plural is not met by one
say the opposite: only one fledgling or one egg -- one is exempt from sending
תא שמע: thief and robber are included in lashes per R' Yehuda, and robbery is a prohibition converted to a positive command -- שמע מינה he flogs for such a prohibition
the baraita: a thief and a robber are included in lashes -- the words of R' Yehuda
R' Zeira: a baraita not taught in the houses of R' Chiyya and R' Oshaya is corrupt and may not be cited; perhaps it taught 'is NOT included in forty lashes' (141b.1)
R' Zeira: any baraita not taught in the houses of R' Chiyya and R' Oshaya is corrupt, and you may not object from it in the study hall
one who takes the mother with the young -- R' Yehuda: he is flogged and does not send
horn 1: R' Yehuda's reason [for lashes] is that he holds one is flogged for a prohibition converted to a positive command
horn 2: in general he holds one is not flogged for a prohibition converted to a positive command, and here the reason is that he holds 'shaleach' means from the outset
הואיל ואמר מר: גדול שלום שבין איש לאשתו
שהרי אמרה תורה: שמו של הקדוש ברוך הוא שנכתב בקדושה ימחה על המים
מאי אולמיה דהאי עשה מהאי עשה? -- why should the other positive command be stronger than this one?
סלקא דעתך, הואיל ואמר מר גדול שלום שבין איש לאשתו... והאי מצורע... אסור בתשמיש המטה -- the metzora's purification restores marital peace
the Master: great is peace between a man and his wife
כיון דאסור בתשמיש המטה
דכתיב: וישב מחוץ לאהלו שבעת ימים -- אהלו זו אשתו, מכאן שאסור בתשמיש המטה
'and he shall dwell outside his tent seven days' (Lev 14:8) -- 'his tent' is his wife
ואימא: שלח -- חדא זימנא, תשלח -- תרי זימני -- the doubled verb yields two sendings, not four or five
but say: 'shalle'ach' -- once, 'teshallach' -- twice
אמר ליה: שלח -- אפילו מאה פעמים; תשלח -- for a matter of mitzva (= p_rava_shaleach_meah, p_rava_teshalach_mitzva)
Rava: 'shalle'ach' -- even a hundred times
הניחא למאן דתני קיימו ולא קיימו (there the answer works); אלא למאן דתני ביטלו ולא ביטלו -- כמה דלא שחטה לא עבריה ללאו: the negative is not yet spent, so the case the answer names has both commands
the one who teaches [the criterion as] 'he annulled it / did not annul it'
ועוד, לרבי יהודה דאמר שלח מעיקרא משמע -- אפילו עשה נמי ליכא: once he took her, even the positive is gone, so there is nothing for 'teshallach' to teach
R' Yehuda, who said: 'shalle'ach' means from the outset
the mishna: sent away and returned, even four or five times -- obligated, as it is said 'shalle'ach teshallach the mother'
שנאמר שלח תשלח את האם
שנאמר שלח תשלח את האם
it is a positive and a negative command, and a positive command does not override a negative-and-positive command

it is needed where he transgressed and took the mother: the negative he has [already] transgressed, only the positive remains; [one might say] let a positive come and override a positive -- [the verse] teaches us [otherwise]
the one who teaches [the criterion for a negative command linked to a positive as] 'he fulfilled it / did not fulfil it'
Mar bar Rav Ashi: e.g. where he took her in order to send her away: there is no negative, there is a positive; and [one might say] let a positive come and override a positive
